ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle, point D is a point on side AB, an equilateral $\triangle CDE$ is constructed upwards with CD as its side, and AE is connected. $\triangle BCD \cong \triangle ACE$. If $AE=1$, $AB=3$, what is the length of $AD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\triangle BCD \cong \triangle ACE$, $AE=1$, $AB=3$,\\
$\therefore$ $BD=AE=1$,\\
$\therefore$ $AD=AB-BD=3-1=\boxed{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ the length of $AD$ is \boxed{2}.
